name: equal best scores: the lower observation id is the best candidate, not the earlier one
notes: §8 (v1.3): grade's best candidate is the highest exact score, ties broken by observation id, so match.best names the assigned candidate whenever one is assigned (§4.3 breaks assignment ties by claimedAt, claim id, then observation id, lowest first). Candidates are ordered by (occurredAt, id, contentHash) (§4.1), so 'the first best in candidate order' would pick the earlier observation instead.
Address claims with a subject: applicable timeProximity 2500, counterpartyExact 3500, counterpartyDomain 1500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 9000. The grant binds gmail.sent to acct-a.

c1 priya@company.com 'Q3 deck' at 14:02 (unit [14:02, 14:03]). o1 (14:03) and o2 (14:02) both carry priya@company.com 'Q3 deck' and lie inside the unit → Δ 0, tp 1, ce 1, cd 1, subject 1 → both 1/1. Tie on score, on claimedAt and on claim → lower observation id: assertIds pins id(o1) < id(o2), although o1 occurred a minute later → c1 takes o1 → verified, FINAL, match.best o1. o2 is an orphan with no activity → no receipt.

c2 raj@company.com 'Budget' at 16:02. o3 (16:03) and o4 (16:02) carry lee@other.example 'Budget': tp 1, ce 0, cd 0 (another domain), subject 1 → S = (2500 + 1500)/9000 = 4/9 each, below partial → neither is assigned. The best candidate is still named (§8): the tie goes to the lower id, o3 (assertIds), the later one → not_found (full coverage, graceElapsed), FINAL, match.best o3, no evidence.
FINAL: the gmail.sent sync at 17:00 ≥ every end + 45. The pairs are two hours apart.
